title: What makes motion hard to stop?
target: Compare momentum changes in a controlled stopping situation.
criteria: Compare mass and velocity while controlling other variables.
Use momentum change to compare stopping force for equal times.
Avoid claiming that momentum alone determines damage.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Two carts have equal velocity. One has four times the mass. Compare momentum magnitudes.
options: The lighter cart has four times the momentum.
The heavier cart has four times the momentum.
cpa.guide: p = mv scales with mass at fixed velocity.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two identical carts move at 2 m/s and 5 m/s in the same direction. Which has greater momentum?
options: The 5 m/s cart, by a factor of 2.5.
The 5 m/s cart, by a factor of 6.25.
The 2 m/s cart, by a factor of 2.5.
cpa.guide: At equal mass, momentum scales linearly with speed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 4 kg cart moving at +3 m/s stops in 2 s. What is average net stopping force?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two objects lose momentum magnitudes of 18 and 6 kg·m/s in the same stopping time. Compare average force magnitudes.
options: The second experiences three times the force.
The first experiences three times the force.
The first experiences nine times the force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two objects have equal momentum magnitudes. What additional information is needed to compare average stopping forces?
cpa.guide: Equal Δp can occur with different force magnitudes over different times.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Equal-momentum impacts damage different surfaces differently. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Momentum alone does not determine damage; contact time, area, and materials matter.
cpa.guide: A momentum account constrains impulse but not every local effect.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
